detail:
MedlinePlus describes chronic low back pain as pain in the lower back that persists for 12 weeks or longer, sometimes after an initial injury or underlying cause has been treated. Low back pain is described as very common, and in many cases no single structural cause is identified. Sources note that persistent pain can involve a combination of mechanical strain, disc and joint changes, nerve irritation, deconditioning, and the way the nervous system processes pain signals over time.

MedlinePlus notes that symptoms can include a dull, aching pain in the lower back, pain that travels into the buttock or leg, stiffness and reduced range of motion, and difficulty standing straight or moving comfortably. Clinicians usually evaluate chronic low back pain using medical history and a physical exam, and imaging or other tests are generally reserved for cases with specific warning signs, neurological findings, or pain that does not improve as expected, rather than ordered routinely for every case.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about chronic low back pain symptoms and evaluation.
summary: MedlinePlus describes chronic low back pain as lower back pain lasting 12 weeks or longer, often without a single identified cause, and evaluated mainly through history and physical examination.
takeaways: chronic low back pain is defined by duration of 12 weeks or longer
symptoms can include aching pain, stiffness, and pain into the leg
imaging is generally reserved for specific signs, not routine cases
title: Chronic Low Back Pain: when lower back pain lasts for months
